names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 13 Οκτωβρίου, «Αγία Χρυσή η Νεομάρτυς», with the rank word left off.

The heading of days.pravoslavie.ru's name page 2751, «Хриса (Хрисия, Злата) Могленская, мц.», with the rank word left off. It carries all three Russian forms of the name; its life heads her «Святая Злата (Хриса) Мегленская» with the other spelling of the epithet.

feast.note: Her repose, as the Russian calendar's 18 October prints it. Her index page keeps one other day, «13 октября (Воспоминание чуда)» — the remembrance of a miracle of hers at Skopje in 1912, which that day's line gives as «Воспоминание чуда вмц. Златы (Хрисы) в Скопье (1912)» (https://days.pravoslavie.ru/Days/20261013.html, read 4 October 2026). One row per church is the schema, so the October 13th is recorded here and she does not render on it. saint.gr puts her death itself on 13 October.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 18 октября ст. ст. — «Преставление вмц. Златы (Хрисы) (1795) (Болг.).»
source.note: No rank is read onto her. The 18 October page's two icons both stand in its first paragraph — a polyeleos before the apostle and evangelist Luke, and the plain service before the finding of Joseph of Volotsk's relics — and her line is in the second. «(Болг.)» on that line marks her as a saint of the Bulgarian church.

attestations.note: The Russian keeps her repose five days after the day the Greek keeps her death on, and its index page keeps both days for her for two different reasons: the repose on 18 October and the remembrance of a miracle at Skopje on 13 October. Its life gives the village the Greek does not name — «болгарском селении Слатино, Могленской епархии», Slatino in the diocese of Moglena — the Turkish yoke Bulgaria lay under, and the local Turk who tried again and again to win her over and make her accept Islam, and whom neither persuasion nor threats nor monstrous torture through many months got anywhere with.
Not checked: doxologia.ro's calendar for the same civil day (1 October 2026).

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 13ης Οκτωβρίου — «Αγία Χρυσή η Νεομάρτυς»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 13 Οκτωβρίου εκάστου έτους» and «Αγια Χρυση η Νεομαρτυς (; - 1795)». The year of her death is stated outright in the life as well — «Τελικά στις 13 Οκτωβρίου 1795 μ.Χ., κατέκοψαν το σώμα της με μαχαίρια» — and a `dates` object carries it. The village is named twice over, «στο χωριό Σλάτενα (σημερινή Χρυσή) της επαρχίας Αλμωπίας Νομού Πέλλης», and the display name takes the older of the two forms because the newer one is her own name and would read as no epithet at all. `locations` is left out all the same, in keeping with the rest of this reader's days. The corpus's `chryse-the-martyr`, kept on the Greek 30 January with her servant `sabainos-the-martyr`, is an ancient martyr and not this woman. Two hymns are taken, an apolytikion and a kontakion, both of which name her; the Μεγαλυνάριον, which also names her, is neither a troparion nor a kontakion and is not drafted. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence on the life page.
Not checked: the Ohrid Prologue on pravoslavno.rs for the corresponding Julian day (1 October 2026).

death.note: saint.gr: «Τελικά στις 13 Οκτωβρίου 1795 μ.Χ., κατέκοψαν το σώμα της με μαχαίρια», and its page head gives her as «Αγια Χρυση η Νεομαρτυς (; - 1795)». days.pravoslavie.ru gives the same year and a different day for it: its life closes «(+ 1795)» and its 18 October line reads «Преставление вмц. Златы (Хрисы) (1795) (Болг.)», where saint.gr puts the death on 13 October 1795. The year is not in dispute and the day is recorded in the attestations.

hymns.text: Σκεῦος χρύσεον, τῆς παρθενίας, καὶ ἀκήρατος, νύμφη Κυρίου, ἐχρημάτισας Χρυσῆ καλλιπάρθενε· τὴν γὰρ ἁγνείαν ἀμέμπτως φυλάττουσα, ὐπὲρ Χριστοῦ θεοφρόνως ἐνήθλησας· Μάρτυς ἔνδοξε, ἱκέτευε τὸν Νυμφίον σου, δωρήσασθε ἡμῖν τὸ μέγα ἔλεος.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἦχος γ’, Θείας Πίστεως — the first hymn on the page of «Αγία Χρυσή η Νεομάρτυς», and it names her.

english.text: You were made a golden vessel of virginity and an undefiled bride of the Lord, Chryse, fair virgin; for keeping your purity blamelessly you contended for Christ with a God-minded heart. Glorious Martyr, entreat your Bridegroom to grant us his great mercy.

hymns.text: Χρυσωθεῖσα Πνεύματι, Τῷ Παναγίῳ, τὴν ἁγνείαν ἔφθορον, τὴν σὴν ἐτήρησας Χριστῷ, καὶ ὑπὲρ φύσιν ἠγώνισαι, παρθενομάρτυς, Χρυσῆ ἀξιάγαστε.

source.text: saint.gr, Κοντάκιον, Ἦχος δ’, Ἐπεφάνης σήμερον — on the page of «Αγία Χρυσή η Νεομάρτυς». It names her and no other saint.

english.text: Gilded by the All-Holy Spirit, you kept your purity incorrupt for Christ and contended beyond nature, virgin-martyr Chryse, worthy of all wonder.
